points.description: States that a leaf is a node (of a tree) that has no children, using the term 'node' and 'no children' (or equivalently 'zero child nodes'/'no descendants').
points.partial_credit: 1.5 if only 'a node at the end/bottom of the tree' or 'node with no children' without clearly identifying it as a node of a tree; otherwise none

points.description: Precise terminology: identifies the leaf as a node in a tree (tree/binary tree context) and states its degree is zero / both child pointers are null (not merely 'last element' or 'end').
Correct distinction from related nodes: a leaf differs from an internal node (a node with at least one child) and from the root; a leaf is not defined by being the last-inserted or rightmost node.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise statement that a leaf is a node with no children, using correct terms. Vague phrasing such as 'the end of the tree' or 'last element' earns nothing for that point. Any wrong claim (e.g., a leaf has one child, or a leaf is the root only) removes the point it affects. The distinction point needs an explicit contrast with internal nodes.
